hypotheses.reasoning: The fault originates at the third-party email provider api.mailer.example, which began returning 503/502 at 13:24:55 (#135), with no earlier anomalies in any service. template-svc's calls to it failed fast (5xx, not hangs), and the circuit breaker opened at 13:26:22 (99% failure rate) and repeatedly re-opened on half-open probes (#153, #190) because the provider stayed down. notification-svc then failed its TemplateClient.render calls with 'template-svc returned 503 (circuit open)' (#158, #165, #178, #187), and the gateway returned 503 on POST /v1/notify with 7-28s latency (#136, #152, #162, #172, #180, #184, #189). The gateway 503s and notification-svc errors are downstream symptoms and are not cited as root evidence. Normal /render calls succeeded until the outage (e.g. #155, #169), and redis, notif-db and notif-worker show no errors, so the local stack is healthy. The GC pauses and TLS-expiry warning are unrelated noise.

Alternative reading: the mailer calls hung and were cut off, which would make this a dependency_timeout. The logs show fast explicit 503/502 responses rather than timeouts, and the gateway latency (7-28s) comes from notification-svc's retries and waiting rather than from a timeout message, so this reading is weaker.

verdict.recommendedAction: Treat this as a third-party outage. Confirm the status of api.mailer.example with the provider and its status page. Meanwhile, consider failing over to a secondary email provider or queuing notifications for later delivery. Keep the template-svc circuit breaker in place so it does not hammer the provider, and reduce gateway-side retries so requests fail fast. Once the mailer recovers, verify that the breaker closes and the 503 rate on /v1/notify returns to baseline.
